summary: Karuna Kusalasaya (1920–2009) worked in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University and as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunapati Tripathi was an Indologist who taught Harish Chandra Mani Tripathi. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and as President of the Uttar Pradesh Sanskrit Sansthan.

Karunesh Shukla (b. 1940), an Indologist and philosopher of Buddhist studies, studied under V. P. Upadhyaya and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation. At Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University, he served as Reader (attested 1973) and later Professor and Head (attested 1991).

Karénina Kollmar-Paulenz (b. 1958) is a scholar of Tibetology, Central Asian studies, and religious studies. She completed her studies, PhD (-1991), and Habilitation at the University of Bonn, later serving at the University of Bern as Professor (1999), Dean (2007–2010), and Emerita (~2023).

Kashi Prasad Jayaswal (1881–1937) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Allahabad, Jesus College, Oxford (M.A. ~1906–1909), and Lincoln's Inn. He served as Tagore Professor of Law at the University of Calcutta (1917) and President of the Numismatic Society of India.

Kashinath Narayan Dikshit (1889–1944) was an Indologist and archaeologist who held posts at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, the Government of India as Offg. Government Epigraphist (~1930–1932), and the Archaeological Survey of India as Deputy Director-General (1937–1944).

Kashinath Trimbak Telang (1850–1893) was an Indologist who studied at Elphinstone College and the University of Mumbai. He served as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Elphinstone College, President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai, and Syndic and Vice-Chancellor (1892–1893) at the University of Mumbai.

Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar (1890–1976) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who taught Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla and Masaaki Hattori. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Gujarat College (~1914–1945) and Honorary Professor of Sanskrit at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (attested 1957).

Kasten Anders Rönnow (1897–1943) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Uppsala University under Jarl Charpentier. He later served as Acting Professor at Uppsala University (1928) and Lund University (1932–1933).

Katarzyna Marciniak is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar based at the University of Warsaw, where she served as a Postdoctorate Researcher at the Research Centre of Buddhist Studies (attested 2016) and as an adjunct (2020).

Kate Crosby is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Oxford, Hamburg, and Kelaniya. She has held posts at Oxford (Professor, 2022), SOAS, King's College London (-2022), Cardiff University, and the Buddhist Institute (2003).

Kate Wharton is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London (-2008) and was affiliated with Birkbeck, University of London (attested 2010).

Katharina Sabernig is a Tibetology scholar who studied at the Medical University of Vienna (MD 1997–2008) and the University of Vienna (PhD 2007–2017). She has held a post at the Medical University of Vienna.
Katharine von Garnier-Moewes (1863–1936) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Leipzig and earned her PhD from Heidelberg University in 1907.
Katherine Anne Narraway is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned her Master of Arts degree at McGill University under the supervision of G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Katherine Anne Paul is a scholar in Tibetology, Indology, and history/archaeology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Gudrun Bühnemann and teachers Tsetan Chonjore, Pasang Dhondup, Nawang Dorji, Gautam Vajracharya, Rama Joshi, and Geeta Manandhar.

Katherine Janiec Jones is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied at Davidson College and completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under Paul J. Griffiths, having also studied under William K. Mahony and Karl A. Plank.

Katherine K. Young (b. 1944) is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned an M.A. from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. from McGill University. She became a professor at McGill University (~1978) and taught Barbra R. Clayton.

Kathleen D. Morrison (b. 1963) is an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at the universities of Notre Dame, New Mexico, and UC Berkeley (PhD 1992), she taught as Assistant Professor at Northwestern University (~1993–1996) and became Professor at the University of Pennsylvania in 2017.

Kathleen Gough (1925–1990) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed her Ph.D. at Girton College, Cambridge (1943–1950). She held posts at Brandeis, the University of Oregon, Simon Fraser University, and the University of British Columbia (1970).
